source_text: Ἡμεῖς δὲ μετὰ τὸ οὕτως λοῦσαι τὸν πεπεισμένον καὶ συγκατατεθειμένον ἐπὶ τοὺς λεγομένους ἀδελφοὺς ἄγομεν, ἔνθα συνηγμένοι εἰσί, κοινὰς εὐχὰς ποιησόμενοι ὑπέρ τε ἑαυτῶν καὶ τοῦ φωτισθέντος καὶ ἄλλων πανταχοῦ πάντων εὐτόνως, ὅπως καταξιωθῶμεν τὰ ἀληθῆ μαθόντες καὶ δι᾿ ἔργων ἀγαθοὶ πολιτευταὶ καὶ φύλακες τῶν ἐντεταλμένων εὑρεθῆναι, ὅπως τὴν αἰώνιον σωτηρίαν σωθῶμεν. Ἀλλήλους φιλήματι ἀσπαζόμεθα παυσάμενοι τῶν εὐχῶν. Ἔπειτα προσφέρεται τῷ προεστῶτι τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἄρτος καὶ ποτήριον ὕδατος καὶ κράματος, καὶ οὗτος λαβὼν αἶνον καὶ δόξαν τῷ πατρὶ τῶν ὅλων διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου ἀναπέμπει καὶ εὐχαριστίαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ κατηξιῶσθαι τούτων παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πολὺ ποιεῖται· οὗ συντελέσαντος τὰς εὐχὰς καὶ τὴν εὐχαριστίαν πᾶς ὁ παρὼν λαὸς ἐπευφημεῖ λέγων· Ἀμήν. Τὸ δὲ ἀμὴν τῇ ἑβραΐδι φωνῇ τὸ γένοιτο σημαίνει. Εὐχαριστήσαντος δὲ τοῦ προεστῶτος καὶ ἐπευφημήσαντος παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ οἱ καλούμενοι παρ᾿ ἡμῖν διάκονοι διδόασιν ἑκάστῳ τῶν παρόντων μεταλαβεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ εὐχαριστηθέντος ἄρτου καὶ οἴνου καὶ ὕδατος καὶ τοῖς οὐ παροῦσιν ἀποφέρουσι.
pass_a_gloss: We, however, after having thus washed the one who has been convinced and has assented to the things concerning the so-called brothers, lead him to where they are gathered, and we offer common prayers for themselves and for the one who has been enlightened and for all others everywhere, that we, having learned the true things, may be found to be good citizens and guardians of the things entrusted, so that we may be saved for eternal salvation. We greet one another with a kiss after ceasing from the prayers. Then bread and a cup of water and wine are offered to the one presiding over the brothers, and he, having taken praise and glory to the Father of all through the name of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, sends it up and gives thanks for being deemed worthy of these things by Him for a long time; and when he has completed the prayers and the thanksgiving, the whole present people applaud, saying: Amen. Now the Amen in the Hebrew language means 'so be it'. And when the presiding one has given thanks and the whole people have applauded, the ones called deacons by us give to each of the present ones to partake of the bread and wine and water that have been given thanks for, and they carry it away to those who are not present.

choices.english: a cup of water and wine
rejected: a cup of water, and a cup of wine

choices.why: conveys the sense of loud approval

pass_b_english: After washing the person who has been convinced and has assented to our teaching, we bring him to the assembly of those called brothers. There, gathered together, we offer common prayers for ourselves, for the one who has been enlightened, and for all others everywhere, that we may be found worthy, having learned the true things, to live as good citizens and guardians of the commandments entrusted to us, so that we may obtain eternal salvation. We greet one another with a kiss when the prayers are ended.

Then bread and a cup of water mixed with wine are brought to the president of the brothers. He takes them and offers praise and glory to the Father of all through the name of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, giving thanks at length for being counted worthy to receive these gifts from Him. When he has finished the prayers and the thanksgiving, all the people present give their assent, saying: Amen. Amen in Hebrew means 'so be it.' After the president has given thanks and the whole congregation has assented, those we call deacons give each person present a share of the bread, wine, and water over which thanks has been given, and they carry portions to those who are absent.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both fail to accurately translate the Greek regarding the content of the cup. The Greek specifies 'ποτήριον ὕδατος καὶ κράματος' (a cup of water and wine/mixed drink). Pass A translates this as 'a cup of water and wine', which is acceptable, but Pass B translates it as 'a cup of water mixed with wine'. While 'κράμα' often implies a mixture, the Greek text provides two distinct substances (water and wine/mixed drink) for the cup. More critically, Pass A omits the word 'κράματος' (wine/mixed drink) in its description of the elements being given to the deacons: 'partake of the bread and wine and water', whereas the Greek is 'ἄρτου καὶ οἴνου καὶ ὕδατος'. While the order is swapped, Pass A's earlier translation of 'ποτήριον ὕδατος καὶ κράματος' as 'a cup of water and wine' is acceptable, but Pass B's interpretation of the cup as 'water mixed with wine' is an interpretive addition not strictly present in the syntax of the Greek 'ὕδατος καὶ κράματος'. However, the primary failure is in Pass A: it translates 'ἔνθα συνηγμένοι εἰσί' as 'to where they are gathered', but the Greek 'ἐπὶ τοὺς λεγομένους ἀδελφοὺς' (concerning/to the so-called brothers) is rendered in Pass A as 'concerning the so-called brothers', which is a correct gloss for 'ἐπὶ', but the phrase 'the one who has been convinced and has assented to the things concerning the so-called brothers' is a misreading of the Greek syntax. The Greek 'πεπεισμένον καὶ συγκατατεθειμένον ἐπὶ τοὺς λεγομένους ἀδελφοὺς' means the person has been convinced and has assented *to* the so-called brothers (or to the matter of them), but Pass A's phrasing 'assented to the things concerning the so-called brothers' adds 'the things' (τὰ) which is not in the Greek text. Furthermore, Pass B adds 'our teaching' ('assented to our teaching') which is not in the Greek text ('συγκατατεθειμένον ἐπὶ τοὺς λεγομένους ἀδελφοὺς').
reasons: Pass A adds 'the things' to 'assented to the things concerning the so-called brothers' (συγκατατεθειμένον ἐπὶ τοὺς λεγομένους ἀδελφοὺς) which is not in the Greek.
Pass B adds 'our teaching' ('assented to our teaching') which is not in the Greek (συγκατατεθειμένον ἐπὶ τοὺς λεγομένους ἀδελφοὺς).
